root_causes.description: The checkout service container was killed/restarted during the window, evidenced by Kubernetes 'Killing: Container checkout definition changed, will be restarted' plus extra Created/Started events, consistent with a pod crash. The checkout pod's working-set memory shows a pronounced anomaly (p50 ~0.55 MB vs max ~25.3 MB) around the restart, and no application error traces/logs were emitted, consistent with an abrupt process termination.

evidence.query_or_id: Killing: Container checkout definition changed, will be restarted

evidence.expected_baseline: 1 steady-state start; extra start indicates a restart
0 restarts; sampling gap is consistent with crash/restart between scrape intervals
< 0.01; absent errors consistent with abrupt process kill

root_causes.description: Alternative interpretation: checkout experienced memory stress, with working-set bytes spiking from a ~0.55 MB median to a ~25.3 MB peak during the window, potentially triggering an OOM-style termination of the container.

Weaker hypothesis: checkout's downstream dependency interactions (cart, payment, email, shipping, currency, product-catalog) could have caused failed requests, but no error traces or error logs were observed, and checkout error_rate remained 0.000, so this is not supported by evidence.

evidence.expected_baseline: error traces present if dependency calls were failing
error/failure log lines if downstream calls were failing
steady checkout request rate; reduced throughput consistent with downtime from a crash

remediation_steps: Confirm checkout pod termination reason and exit code (kubectl describe pod) to distinguish OOMKilled from a generic crash/restart.
Raise the checkout container memory request/limit to accommodate the observed ~25 MB peak working set and enable a memory-based alert.
Verify/add liveness and readiness probes so restarts drain traffic gracefully and avoid request loss.
Investigate the repeated pause-container image pull failures (ImagePullBackOff) that can delay the container restart recovery.
Monitor checkout restart counts and memory working set for recurrence over the next window.
